items.title: Russian Civilian Deaths Are Growing Rapidly as Ukraine Expands Its Air War
items.summary: The higher tempo of Ukrainian strikes has fueled discontent among Russians, but it is far from clear that it will change the Kremlin’s calculus about the war.

items.title: A Syrian Holdout Province, Sweida, Fears a Government Takeover
items.summary: In Sweida Province, dominated by the country’s Druse minority, many say it is just a matter of time before the central government moves to assert control over the region.

items.title: What We Know About the Earthquake in Colombia
items.summary: The 7.4-magnitude quake, which killed more than 100 people and damaged hundreds of buildings, was the strongest recorded in Colombia in a decade.

items.title: The Eclipse Is Coming, and Iceland Is … Mostly Ready
items.summary: Rooms were booked years ago, and officials have been making plans. But there’s no telling where, exactly, Icelanders might go to find the best possible view.

items.title: Spain’s Complex Ties With Morocco Fuel Speculation Over Ceuta Migrant Surge
items.summary: Rumors swirled that Morocco, perhaps spurred by Israel and the United States, organized a recent border disaster. That unproven speculation, experts said, was exacerbated by the region’s complicated history.

items.title: How Raúl Castro’s Grandson, Raúl G. Rodríguez Castro, Became a Power Broker
items.summary: The Castro family envoy, Raúl G. Rodríguez Castro, who has been in talks with the Trump administration, was once named in a case targeting a Cuban smuggling ring.

items.title: What to Know About the Cuban Mafia in Quintana Roo
items.summary: A group of Cuban men in Mexico was charged with smuggling people to the United States. One of its leaders said Raúl Castro’s grandson helped, according to interviews and court records.

items.title: In a Sweltering Summer, These Italians Want Romans to Curl
items.summary: By setting up a curling rink in the shadow of the Colosseum, sports officials hope to capitalize on the fresh popularity of the Winter Olympics phenomenon. Even in a heat wave and without any ice.

items.title: France Bans Unsolicited Telemarketing Calls
items.summary: Companies will no longer be allowed to advertise goods and services through cold calls without previous consent from consumers.

items.title: Major Quake Hits Colombia, Killing at Least 111
items.summary: Rescue crews and regular people searched for survivors, and the death toll was likely to rise. More than 1,500 homes were damaged, the president said.

items.title: The Perils of Wall St.’s Race to Pour Billions More Into A.I.
items.summary: Investors including BlackRock have committed an eye-popping amount to lend to the artificial intelligence industry. That enthusiasm isn’t shared by everyone.

items.title: Oil Prices Rise to $90 a Barrel Over U.S.-Iran Stalemate
items.summary: The stalemate over the Iran war hardened and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz continued to dwindle.

items.title: In a Summer of Climate Misery, Businesses Confront the Need to Adapt
items.summary: Repeated heat waves, wildfires, droughts and storms are solidifying the understanding that new investments are unavoidable.

items.title: How Social Media Sparked a Refugee Crisis Between Spain and Morocco
items.summary: A wave of disinformation online contributed to a surge of migrants in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta who were trying to reach Europe, resulting in about 90 deaths.

items.title: Should You Be Dating While Unemployed?
items.summary: If you’re single and unemployed, it may make sense to prioritize job hunting. But that doesn’t have to mean putting your life on pause.

items.title: As Credit Card Debt Mounts, Home Becomes a Piggy Bank
items.summary: A rise in home equity to record levels has led many Americans to refinance their mortgages to pay their bills.

items.title: Wall St. Wants Another Half-Trillion Dollars for the A.I. Boom
items.summary: Six giant investment firms announced a $500 billion effort to raise money for customers of Nvidia to pay for computing power.

items.title: Traffic to Trump’s Truth Social Falls Sharply This Summer
items.summary: President Trump’s social media platform has had double-digit declines in visitors in June and July, according to estimates from a widely cited online tracking firm.

items.title: Trump Shrugs Off A.I. and Data Center Concerns as Voters Grow Anxious
items.summary: The president and his top aides have been especially bullish about data centers, despite national blowback against the facilities.

items.title: How Small, Independent Newspapers Are Still Finding Readers
items.summary: In a world of failing newspapers, free weeklies like The Chronicle of Glens Falls, N.Y., are still finding readers. All it takes is owners who do absolutely everything.

items.title: Waymo Is Growing Faster Than Ever. So Are Its ‘Edge Cases.’
items.summary: As Waymo deploys more driverless cars to 15 U.S. cities and counting, its vehicles keep encountering new and unexpected situations that they have no script to handle.

items.title: A.I.-Driven Chip Crunch Leads to New Rush of Lobbying in Washington
items.summary: As data centers gobble up memory chips, other industries that need the components, including electronics companies like Apple and medical device makers, are asking for government help.

items.title: Meta Unveils an Open Version of Its Most Powerful A.I. Model
items.summary: The release of Muse Glimmer, a model that can be freely downloaded and modified, is likely to intensify a debate over whether A.I. should be restricted.

items.title: Flock Cameras Can Track Every Car in America. Police Love Them. Citizens Don’t.
items.summary: In Texas, there’s one thing liberals and conservatives agree on: They don’t want cameras trained on their cars.

items.title: His Start-Up’s Goal: A.I. That Is Trainable and Not Controlled by a Big Company
items.summary: A co-founder of xAI is going all in on building open-source artificial intelligence so that “anyone can control and shape A.I. for their own needs.”

items.title: Can A.I. Get You Where You Want to Go for Less?
items.summary: A wave of new services uses A.I. to monitor flights and hotel reservations to help you find lower prices. We look at how these tools work.

items.title: Why Are So Many People Upset About Flock Cameras?
items.summary: Flock Safety’s automated license plate-reading cameras, used by thousands of law enforcement agencies in the U.S., have drawn intense criticism from civil liberties groups.

items.title: The Surprising Truth About Instagram’s VHS Dates Videos
items.summary: VHS Dates advertises itself as resurfacing lost dating service videotapes from the 1980s. The account’s followers have been genuinely touched.

items.title: New Amazon Data Center Stokes Worry It Would Be the Most Polluting Power Plant in the U.S.
items.summary: The tech giant is investing in the natural-gas-burning power plant as part of a huge data center in Texas, even as it pledges to honor climate commitments.
